policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the qere, which is what MACULA Hebrew projects; the alternative is the ketiv written in the Leningrad Codex.

decisions.evidence: ASV renders the qere ולו 'and to/by him': 'And by him actions are weighed' translates the prepositional phrase, not the negative ולא. The verse note ('According to another reading, Though actions be not weighed') places the ketiv ולא outside the text as the alternative, confirming the main text follows r00-base.

ASV 'He will keep the feet of his holy ones' is plural, matching the qere חסידיו; the ketiv חסידו is singular 'his holy one'. The note ('Or, godly ones Another reading is, holy one') is classed alternative_rendering and does not itself decide, but the plural in the ASV text does.

ASV 'They that strive with Jehovah shall be broken to pieces' is plural, rendering the qere plural participle מריביו; the ketiv מריבו is singular 'he that striveth with him'. No mapped note bears on the unit; the number in the English settles it.

Qere עליו and ketiv עלו are plene and defective spellings of the same prepositional phrase; both are read 'against him/them' with the same sense. ASV 'Against them will he thunder in heaven' distinguishes neither, and no note is mapped to this unit, so the qere base fallback carries the projection.

ASV 'then he would say, Nay, but thou shalt give it me now' renders the qere לא as the negative 'Nay'. The mapped textual_variant note ('Another reading is, he would say unto him, Thou etc.') gives the ketiv לו 'unto him' as the reading the ASV did not follow, confirming r00-base in the text.
